title: PSA opening European card grading center during partial submission pause
content:
Trading card grading leader Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) will begin accepting submissions at its first full-scale European grading center in Frankfurt, Germany, in July, the company announced Thursday. PSA first announced plans to open the facility alongside expanded operations in Canada and Japan last September.

Initial submissions, which are projected to open on July 15, will be limited to PSA Authorized Dealers and other partners, with grading planned to begin in August. Opening to all customers is expected later this year. PSA Europe will accept the majority of sports cards and trading card games (TCG), including Pokémon, with categories such as tickets and oversized memorabilia forwarded to locations in the United States. PSA plans to hire roughly 100 local employees to staff the Frankfurt facility.

PSA’s expansion into Europe comes amid an unprecedented number of grading submissions to the company’s U.S. operation. PSA paused accepting new submissions through four of its most popular service tiers earlier this month in order to cut into a 10 million-card backlog. That backlog expanded to 14 million cards in the days between PSA announcing the pause on May 28 and those services closing on June 2. PSA estimates it will now take five to six months to trim the backlog to the five-million card mark, where it plans to reopen those impacted service levels. The lowest open card grading tier is currently $79.99 per card with an estimated 40-50 business day turnaround.

PSA Europe will offer the same card grading services as locations in the United States and will be impacted by service pauses when it begins accepting submissions.

According to PSA, overseas submission volume has increased by a more than 100 percent compound annual growth rate over the last five years, and roughly 30 percent of global submissions in May originated internationally. The Frankfurt facility is expected to trim turnaround times for international submissions, which is then expected to hasten turnaround times domestically.

“When factoring in transatlantic shipping, customs processing, etc., we are estimating that turnaround times can improve by more than 30 percent over current projections,” Ryan Miller, head of international for PSA, told The Athletic.

Beckett, which was acquired by PSA parent company Collectors in December, opened its own full-service grading facility in Lage, Germany, in January 2025. CGC Cards, which is currently the second-largest grader by submission volume behind PSA, began grading TCG full-time at its Munich office earlier this year. PSA touted Germany’s growing trading card economy and the country’s centralized position within Europe’s logistical network as reasons for selecting Frankfurt.

In May, Collectors announced plans to invest $200 million into PSA over the next 18 months. That money is expected to help hire more than 1,000 open and planned positions while doubling PSA’s physical footprint globally.

“While there isn’t a specific percentage, opening the Frankfurt facility is the first tangible manifestation of PSA’s $200 million global infrastructure,” Miller said.

PSA graded more than 19 million cards in 2025, according to grading tracker GemRate, and is expected to top 20 million in 2026, with output from January through April up 35 percent year over year.
